fieldValues.title: A protocol with two homes is obeyed from the stale one
fieldValues.summary: When the same process is written down in two places, agents follow whichever they find first, and that is usually the older one. Cloud sessions followed a retired command file over the live trigger prompt for three ticks before anyone noticed.
fieldValues.rationale:
The alternative considered was keeping both homes and adding a note to the retired one saying which was current. It loses because a note is still content an agent can read as instruction, and because the failure was not that the retired file was wrong — it was that it existed and was reachable. So the retired files were reduced to pointers rather than corrected.

What would change this: if a mechanism existed that made staleness structurally visible to a reader — a version the reader must resolve rather than a file it may open — two homes could be safe. Nothing in the current tooling does that, so the rule stands: one live home per protocol, everything else a pointer.
